phases.name: Scope, facts, and assumptions
phases.description: Start from the frozen brief, distinguish its guarantees from design proposals, and identify decisions the prompt leaves open.

phases.name: Instrument services and propagate trace context
phases.description: Model an example request across services, propagate trace context, and export spans asynchronously through a collector tier.

phases.name: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
phases.description: Buffer high-volume telemetry, make trace-level sampling decisions, store queryable spans, archive older data, and derive service dependencies.

phases.name: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
phases.description: Provide a trace query path for trace details, service maps, and latency investigations without coupling reads to ingestion.

phases.name: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
phases.description: Observe overhead, freshness, queue pressure, and query health; then review capacity and policy questions before treating the design as production-ready.

steps.phase: Scope, facts, and assumptions
steps.title: Separate the prompt from the design
steps.content: The frozen brief asks for tracing requests across distributed services, capturing timing and latency, visualizing service dependencies, sampling traces, storing and querying trace data, identifying bottlenecks, handling billions of spans per day, and integrating different frameworks. Its constraints are low application overhead, high trace volume, efficient storage, trace-context propagation, and real-time analysis. It does not specify a numeric ingest rate, peak-to-average ratio, latency SLO, retention period, sampling policy, deployment provider, or supported framework list. The fixture records has_guided_walkthrough=false; that is the frozen snapshot value, not a fresh AWS check.

steps.phase: Scope, facts, and assumptions
steps.title: Mark assumptions and open questions
steps.content: Design assumptions (proposals, not facts from the brief): use vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry APIs and OTLP; propagate W3C Trace Context; separate asynchronous span ingestion from interactive queries; partition buffered work by trace ID where trace-level decisions require co-location; keep recent searchable spans separately from a lower-cost archive; and derive service maps from observed spans. Open questions: what does “real-time” mean for ingest, search, and service maps; what are peak spans/second and span-size distributions; which languages and framework versions must be supported; which attributes are sensitive; what retention and deletion rules apply; what sampling bias is acceptable; and what regional recovery objectives are required? No numeric SLO, retention, or sampling rate is assumed here.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Add an instrumented request entry point
steps.content: Represent the example application entry point as instrumented. Its gateway instrumentation creates or continues a trace, records request timing and status, and forwards trace context to downstream services. This is the workload being observed, not a tracing-product ingress API.

component.label: Instrumented Application Gateway
component.description: Example request entry point with trace-context propagation

properties.purpose: Represent the observed application's request entry point; create or continue trace context, record request timing and outcome, and propagate context to downstream services.

component.highlightReason: The existing API Gateway catalog component models the example application's edge; instrumentation is configuration of that component, not a new product-specific node.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Add the first instrumented service
steps.content: Model a representative application service with framework instrumentation. The SDK should record bounded span attributes and duration/status, use asynchronous batched export, and avoid blocking the user request on telemetry delivery. Framework adapters and auto-instrumentation coverage must be validated for the actual supported runtimes.

component.label: Instrumented Checkout Service
component.description: Example service emitting spans from its application runtime

properties.purpose: Run framework-specific OpenTelemetry instrumentation in-process; create spans for work and dependencies, record duration and outcome, and export asynchronously so telemetry does not block application requests.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Backend Server supports the real service boundary; SDK instrumentation is embedded in the service rather than modeled as an unsupported standalone node.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Add a downstream instrumented service
steps.content: A second service demonstrates that one logical request can produce related spans in multiple processes. It extracts the incoming context, creates child spans, and retains the same trace identity when it calls another service; it must not start an unrelated trace for every hop.

component.label: Instrumented Inventory Service
component.description: Downstream service continuing the distributed trace

properties.purpose: Extract propagated trace context, create child spans for local work, preserve the trace identity across framework boundaries, and export spans asynchronously.

component.highlightReason: A second catalog Backend Server makes cross-service propagation and dependency discovery explicit.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Propagate context from the gateway to the first service
steps.content: Forward the request together with the W3C trace context headers. Validate and continue a well-formed context; define an explicit policy for absent or invalid context so the entry point can start a new trace without trusting arbitrary baggage.

connection.label: Application request + W3C trace context
connection.description: The downstream service continues the same trace and records its own span.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Continue the trace across another service hop
steps.content: Propagate trace context on the downstream call and create a child span at the receiving service. Propagate only reviewed baggage; avoid putting secrets, credentials, or unbounded user data into headers or span attributes.

connection.label: Downstream call + propagated traceparent
connection.description: Parent/child span relationships let a query reconstruct one request across services.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Add a horizontally scalable telemetry front door
steps.content: Put a load-balancing boundary in front of collector instances so exporters can distribute OTLP traffic and the collector tier can scale independently from application services. Health checks and drain behavior should avoid dropping in-flight batches during rollout; exact topology depends on the deployment environment.

component.label: OTLP Ingest Load Balancer
component.description: Distributes telemetry export traffic across collector capacity

properties.purpose: Distribute OTLP exports to healthy collector instances, support controlled draining, and expose collector-tier health for independent scaling.

component.highlightReason: The existing Load Balancer catalog component fits this traffic-distribution boundary without selecting a cloud provider.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Add the OpenTelemetry Collector boundary
steps.content: The current component catalog has no dedicated trace collector or telemetry-ingest component, so use its generic custom component for this missing fit only. The proposed collector validates OTLP, batches and normalizes resource metadata, redacts configured sensitive attributes, and applies bounded buffering before asynchronous delivery. It is not a vendor commitment; collector deployment, processor chain, and failure behavior remain design choices.

component.label: OpenTelemetry Collector Tier
component.description: Vendor-neutral OTLP receive, normalize, redact, and batch boundary

properties.subtitle: Telemetry ingest
properties.purpose: Receive OTLP spans, validate and normalize resource metadata, redact configured sensitive attributes, batch exports, and apply bounded buffering before asynchronous ingestion.
properties.notes: Generic custom node is used because the current catalog has no trace collector component; provider, processor configuration, and deployment topology are open decisions.

component.highlightReason: A focused custom component is justified: the catalog contains monitoring but no trace collector/OTLP ingest fit. All surrounding nodes reuse existing catalog components.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Export gateway spans asynchronously
steps.content: The instrumented gateway exports OTLP batches through the ingest front door. A bounded exporter queue and timeout prevent a slow collector from extending request latency; the application owner's policy must decide whether telemetry is dropped, retried, or locally buffered under sustained failure.

connection.label: Asynchronous OTLP span batches
connection.description: The exporter keeps telemetry delivery off the synchronous application request path.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Export service spans asynchronously
steps.content: Export completed spans in batches over OTLP rather than synchronously calling the tracing query service. Bound queue memory, batch size, retry time, and attribute count according to measured overhead and loss objectives.

connection.label: Batched OTLP spans
connection.description: Service instrumentation exports spans asynchronously to the collector tier.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Export downstream spans with the same trace identity
steps.content: Each participating framework exports spans carrying the shared trace ID and its local span/parent IDs. The collector can then correlate framework-specific instrumentation into one request view; unsupported runtimes need an adapter or explicit instrumentation plan.

connection.label: Batched OTLP spans with trace identity
connection.description: Framework exporters converge on one provider-neutral ingest contract.

steps.phase: Instrument services and propagate trace context
steps.title: Route OTLP traffic into collectors
steps.content: Route authenticated, encrypted OTLP traffic to healthy collector instances. Apply request and payload bounds so malformed or oversized telemetry cannot exhaust ingest capacity; transport and identity mechanisms depend on the deployment environment.

connection.label: Validated OTLP ingest
connection.description: Collector capacity scales independently and receives batches from instrumented runtimes.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Add a durable telemetry buffer
steps.content: Use a broker to absorb bursts and decouple collectors from downstream sampling and storage. Partition by trace ID when the selected trace-level sampler needs all spans for a trace to reach one worker; size partitions, replication, and retention from measured peak volume and recovery objectives rather than catalog defaults.

component.label: Trace Span Stream
component.description: Buffered span stream for burst absorption and consumer isolation

properties.purpose: Buffer normalized span batches, absorb bursts, and isolate collectors from storage consumers; use trace-ID-aware partitioning if trace-level decisions require spans for one trace to co-locate.

component.highlightReason: The existing Message Broker catalog component fits asynchronous high-volume ingestion; no broker vendor or partition count is assumed.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Buffer normalized spans before processing
steps.content: Publish bounded, normalized span records to the stream. Define acknowledgment and retry semantics to avoid silent loss or unbounded duplicates; downstream writes should be idempotent on stable trace/span identifiers.

connection.label: Normalized spans keyed by trace ID
connection.description: The stream absorbs bursts and provides a replay boundary for consumers.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Add a trace-aware processing and sampling tier
steps.content: Consumers group spans by trace identity, handle late arrivals within a bounded decision window, apply the reviewed sampling policy, and write retained traces and derived service edges. A tail-sampling policy can preserve slow or failed traces, but requires state, trace affinity, and a decision delay; head sampling is cheaper but may discard a trace before its outcome is known. The policy and loss budget are open decisions.

component.label: Trace Sampling and Indexing Workers
component.description: Trace-aware sampling, enrichment, indexing, and dependency aggregation

properties.purpose: Group spans by trace ID, handle bounded late arrivals, apply the selected sampling policy, idempotently persist retained spans, and aggregate service-dependency observations.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Processing Worker models asynchronous trace processing; trace-specific behavior is described in its editable purpose.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Scale processing independently from ingestion
steps.content: Workers consume partitions independently and report lag and failures. If tail sampling is enabled, preserve trace affinity and hold spans only for the reviewed decision window; on overload, make the degradation policy observable rather than silently presenting partial traces as complete.

connection.label: Partitioned span batches and replay
connection.description: Consumer scaling and lag are independent from collector capacity.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Add the queryable recent-span store
steps.content: Use a time-oriented store for recent retained spans, with access paths for trace ID and the supported time/service/error filters. The exact physical model, index cardinality, retention, compression, and consistency behavior require workload testing; avoid indexing every arbitrary attribute without a cardinality and cost policy.

component.label: Recent Trace Store
component.description: Queryable retained spans and trace-level indexes

properties.purpose: Persist retained spans and trace indexes for recent trace-ID, time, service, and error queries; choose partitions, indexes, compression, and retention from measured access patterns.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Database supports a Time-Series type, an appropriate generic fit for time-stamped span data without naming a vendor.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Persist selected spans and searchable trace metadata
steps.content: Write a trace's retained spans and searchable metadata using idempotent trace/span keys. Keep writes partition-aware and make sampling status, missing-span indicators, and ingest time available to queries so partial or delayed data is not mistaken for a complete trace.

connection.label: Retained spans + trace indexes
connection.description: The query store is optimized for recent trace retrieval and investigation.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Add lower-cost trace block storage
steps.content: Archive compressed trace blocks or retained raw span batches separately from the hot query index. Lifecycle and deletion rules must keep archive retention consistent with privacy, legal, and customer policies; the brief gives no retention duration or provider.

component.label: Trace Archive
component.description: Compressed trace blocks for policy-governed longer retention

properties.purpose: Store compressed trace blocks outside the hot index for policy-governed retention and replay; lifecycle, encryption, deletion, and provider choices require review.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Object Storage component is a reusable fit for large compressed trace blocks; no provider or retention period is invented.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Archive according to reviewed retention tiers
steps.content: Write compressed or immutable blocks from the processing tier after the sampling decision. Reconciliation should detect archive gaps; lifecycle expiration must honor the final retention and deletion policy rather than a guessed duration.

connection.label: Compressed retained trace blocks
connection.description: The archive separates long-lived bulk data from interactive indexes.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Add a derived service-dependency store
steps.content: Store aggregated service-to-service relationships and time-windowed signals derived from parent/child spans. This is a derived view, not a second source of truth for raw spans; define aggregation windows, edge cardinality, and freshness from query needs.

component.label: Service Dependency Graph
component.description: Derived service edges and time-windowed dependency signals

properties.purpose: Store aggregated service-to-service edges and time-windowed dependency signals derived from spans; remain a rebuildable view rather than the raw-span source of truth.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Database's Graph type fits derived dependency relationships; no standalone unsupported graph product is introduced.

steps.phase: Ingest, sample, persist, and build dependency data
steps.title: Build dependency edges from observed spans
steps.content: Aggregate service identity and parent/child relationships from retained or policy-approved sampled spans. Track the observation window and freshness so the service map distinguishes current topology from historical or incomplete data.

connection.label: Aggregated service edges and latency signals
connection.description: Derived topology supports service maps without scanning all raw spans per view.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Add an independent trace query service
steps.content: Serve trace lookup, time/service/error filters, span waterfalls, and dependency views from a separate stateless API. Enforce tenant authorization and query bounds; avoid unbounded scans across high-cardinality attributes.

component.label: Trace Query API
component.description: Authorized trace retrieval and service-map query orchestration

properties.purpose: Authorize and bound trace-ID, time, service, and error queries; compose span waterfalls and service-map data from hot storage, archive, and derived topology.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Backend Server is the existing fit for the stateless trace-query service.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Add a bounded cache for repeated investigation reads
steps.content: Cache only safe, frequently repeated query results with tenant-aware keys and short, policy-driven freshness. Do not let cache state hide newly arrived spans or bypass authorization; the cache is an optimization and the stores remain authoritative.

component.label: Trace Query Cache
component.description: Bounded cache for repeated trace and dependency queries

properties.purpose: Cache selected repeated trace and service-map query results with tenant-aware keys and reviewed freshness; never bypass authorization or replace authoritative storage.

component.highlightReason: The existing Cache catalog component fits this optional read optimization without requiring a vendor choice.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Add the trace investigation interface
steps.content: Present a trace waterfall with service, duration, parent/child, error, and timing information, plus a service dependency view. Mark sampled, delayed, missing, or partial trace data so an investigator does not mistake absent spans for proof that work did not occur.

component.label: Trace Explorer UI
component.description: Trace waterfall, service map, and bottleneck investigation

properties.purpose: Let authorized users inspect trace waterfalls, service dependencies, latency, and errors while exposing sampling, freshness, and partial-data status.

component.highlightReason: The existing Web App component provides the UI boundary; the trace-specific views are application behavior, not a new catalog component.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Connect the investigator to the query API
steps.content: The UI calls an authenticated query API rather than accessing storage directly. Paginate or bound results, and include timestamps and sampling/freshness metadata in the response contract.

connection.label: Authorized trace and service-map queries
connection.description: The query API enforces access and query bounds before reading storage.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Read recent traces and span details
steps.content: Fetch a trace by identity and retrieve bounded indexed spans for the selected time range. Reassemble parent/child ordering using span identifiers and timestamps, and return missing-span or ingest-lag signals when data is incomplete.

connection.label: Trace ID, time, service, and error lookups
connection.description: Recent indexed spans support interactive trace reconstruction.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Retrieve older trace data under policy
steps.content: When a query falls outside the hot tier, fetch archive blocks only if the caller is authorized and the retention policy permits it. Older-data latency may differ from recent search and should be visible to users rather than hidden behind one implied SLO.

connection.label: Policy-checked older trace retrieval
connection.description: The archive supports retained historical traces with a distinct access path.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Read service relationships and aggregate signals
steps.content: Read the derived service graph for dependency visualization and time-windowed latency/error summaries. Include its observation window and freshness in the response because graph data is aggregated and may lag raw spans.

connection.label: Service map and dependency summaries
connection.description: Aggregated topology supports dependency visualization without a raw-span full scan.

steps.phase: Query traces and diagnose bottlenecks
steps.title: Use the cache without weakening correctness
steps.content: The query API checks the cache for eligible repeated reads, validates tenant and authorization scope, and falls back to authoritative stores on a miss or stale entry. Cache invalidation/freshness should be aligned with ingest delay and the eventual consistency users accept.

connection.label: Tenant-scoped query result cache
connection.description: The cache accelerates eligible reads but is never the source of truth.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Add telemetry-pipeline monitoring
steps.content: Monitor application-side export overhead and drops, collector acceptance/errors, broker age and backlog, sampler decisions, stored-span freshness, archive completeness, and query latency/errors. Alert thresholds must come from agreed service objectives and observed baselines, not from this brief.

component.label: Tracing Platform Monitoring
component.description: Ingest, sampling, storage freshness, and query health

properties.purpose: Observe exporter overhead and drops, collector acceptance, queue age, sampling outcomes, storage freshness, archive completeness, and query latency/errors; set alert thresholds only after objectives are agreed.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Monitoring component supports metrics and alerting; its scope is described in catalog-supported editable properties.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Measure collector health and overhead signals
steps.content: Export collector receive/accepted/rejected counts, batch sizes, processor duration, memory pressure, and exporter failures. Correlate these with application-side instrumentation cost so low overhead is measured end to end rather than inferred from configuration.

connection.label: Collector acceptance, errors, and resource metrics
connection.description: Ingest telemetry exposes collector health and contributes to overhead measurements.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Observe backlog and replay behavior
steps.content: Track queue age, partition skew, consumer lag, replay rate, and redelivery/duplicate rates. These signals distinguish a healthy ingest front door from a downstream pipeline that is quietly falling behind.

connection.label: Queue age, skew, lag, and replay metrics
connection.description: Backlog signals indicate whether sampling and storage consumers keep pace.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Measure sampling decisions and data completeness
steps.content: Report retained/dropped decisions by policy, trace-decision delay, late/missing spans, write failures, and derived-graph freshness. Make policy changes auditable and compare their impact on error and slow-trace discovery.

connection.label: Sampling, processing, and freshness outcomes
connection.description: Processing telemetry reveals sampling behavior and incomplete trace risk.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Measure investigation latency and effectiveness
steps.content: Measure query latency and errors by query class (trace ID, time filters, service map, archive), plus cache hit rate and stale-result behavior. To validate bottleneck identification, test whether known injected slow/error spans can be found and correctly attributed in the UI.

connection.label: Query latency, errors, and result freshness
connection.description: Query telemetry verifies the operational behavior of trace investigation.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Choose sampling with an explicit observability tradeoff
steps.content: Sampling can bound cost, but changes which incidents are visible. Head sampling is fast and low-state but decides before request outcome; tail sampling can retain slow/error traces but needs trace affinity, buffering, and a decision window. A hybrid policy may preserve selected errors or tenant-critical traffic, but rates and rules must be based on measured volume, privacy policy, and an agreed loss budget. Always expose sampling metadata and do not claim unsampled absence proves an event did not happen.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Scale from a measured span envelope
steps.content: “Billions of spans per day” is not a complete capacity plan: burst factor, span size, sampling rate, tenant skew, retention, and query mix are unspecified. Benchmark collection, broker partitions, trace-affine processing, storage indexes, and archive writes separately using representative payloads. Scale each tier from throughput, lag, freshness, and saturation evidence; do not convert the brief into invented capacity numbers.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Define what real-time analysis means
steps.content: The interactive path is: instrumented service → asynchronous export → collector → buffered stream → trace-aware processing → hot span/dependency stores → query API → trace UI. This keeps ingest independent from investigation, but the queue, sampling window, indexing, and graph aggregation add delay. Agree separate freshness and latency objectives for trace-by-ID lookup, filtered search, and service maps before claiming real-time behavior.

steps.phase: Operate at high volume and review open decisions
steps.title: Resolve production decisions before finalizing
steps.content: Open questions: which languages/frameworks and propagation formats are required; what peak spans/second, payload sizes, tenant skew, and query mix should tests represent; what overhead and ingest/query freshness objectives define success; which head/tail/hybrid sampling policy and loss budget are acceptable; which span attributes require redaction and access control; how long hot and archived data must remain and how deletion works; what replication, regional recovery, and replay guarantees are needed; and what trace search dimensions are supported? The graph is a review draft, not a verified production architecture or an AI/browser acceptance result.
